primary_research_scope: dynamic TRSP/WSRP re-planning under delay propagation

solver_strategy.preferred_solver_reason: OR-Tools is the preferred future integration path because it supports C++ integration, routing and constraint programming workflows, and avoids immediate dependence on commercial licensing.
solver_strategy.gurobi_not_required_reason: Gurobi is not required for the current platform stage because licensing, environment, and deployment constraints should not block the research system architecture.
solver_strategy.custom_solver_warning: The project must not depend on implementing a complete industrial-grade TRSP/WSRP solver from scratch before the experimental platform is useful.

solver_candidates.label: OR-Tools adapter
solver_candidates.planned_role: main future solver backend for routing, assignment, scheduling, and constrained re-planning experiments
solver_candidates.notes: This is the preferred integration target once the read-only contracts, experiments, and API boundary are stable.

solver_candidates.label: Internal baseline heuristics
solver_candidates.planned_role: baseline policies, sanity checks, fast deterministic comparisons, and controlled experiments
solver_candidates.notes: These baselines are useful for validating the experimental pipeline before adding an external solver.

solver_candidates.label: Gurobi adapter
solver_candidates.planned_role: future exact or MIP benchmark when licensing and environment constraints are acceptable
solver_candidates.notes: This option must remain optional and must not become a blocker for the platform.

research_alignment.why_solver_is_needed: TRSP and WSRP variants are commonly solved with optimization and constraint-based methods. The platform should therefore integrate mature solvers instead of relying only on hand-written ad hoc algorithms.
research_alignment.why_internal_baselines_still_matter: Internal baselines provide reproducible lower-complexity policies for comparison, regression tests, and sanity checks.
research_alignment.comparative_analysis_role: The solver adapter must support repeated experiments so policies and techniques can be compared by performance, robustness, stability, and computational cost.
research_alignment.statistical_analysis_role: Solver outputs must be exportable to the analysis pipeline for ranking sensitivity, scenario grouping, quality checks, and future statistical comparison.

policy_comparison_requirements: same instance must be reusable across multiple policies
same perturbation set must be reusable across multiple policies
solver output must include feasibility and delay propagation metrics
solver output must include computational time or effort proxy
solver output must include route stability or disruption indicators
solver output must not claim statistical superiority from a single run
safety_requirements: Do not expose solver execution from the browser in the current stage.
Do not claim operational readiness before persisted jobs, validation, rollback, and audit logs exist.
Do not require Gurobi for the project to run.
Do not treat OR-Tools integration as already implemented.
Do not hide licensing or deployment constraints behind the solver abstraction.
Keep the dissertation focus narrow on delay propagation even if the platform remains extensible.

future_milestones.label: Create internal CLI adapter for baseline policies
Create isolated OR-Tools C++ adapter spike
Connect solver outputs to comparative and statistical analysis

conservative_note: This contract documents the intended solver integration architecture. It does not execute OR-Tools, Gurobi, or any optimization job.
safety_note: The current platform remains read-only at the web/API boundary for this artifact.
